Interaction Effect Size: Insulin Resistance Status × Mitigator Type on Peak Glucose Reduction
=============================================================================================

Primary model: peak_glucose ~ mitigator * SSPG (continuous)

  Interaction coefficient (mitigator[T.Protein]:SSPG) = +0.140 mg/dL per unit SSPG
  95% CI: [−0.297, +0.576]
  p-value: 0.520 (not significant)
  Partial eta-squared: 0.012 (small effect size by Cohen's convention)
  n = 19 subjects (38 observations)

Subgroup means (median-split, SSPG > 75 = IR, SSPG <= 75 = IS):

  IS group (n=10): protein peak 150.4 vs fiber peak 162.5 mg/dL → reduction = −12.0 mg/dL
  IR group (n=9):  protein peak 179.8 vs fiber peak 179.0 mg/dL → reduction = +0.7 mg/dL

Spearman correlation (SSPG vs peak reduction): rho = +0.328, p = 0.170

Conclusion: The interaction between baseline insulin resistance (SSPG) and mitigator type (protein vs. fiber preload) on peak postprandial glucose is not statistically significant. The standardized effect size is small (partial eta-squared = 0.012). A weak, non-significant positive trend (rho = 0.328) suggests that more insulin-resistant individuals may derive less glycemic benefit from protein preloading relative to fiber preloading, but the sample (n = 19) is underpowered to resolve this. The null interaction result should be interpreted as inconclusive rather than as evidence of no interaction.

grader_notes: The agent made several methodological errors: using SSPG as primary IR marker instead of DI with SSPG fallback, mishandling replicate averaging (max vs mean) and using absolute peak instead of delta, and reversing the reduction sign. While ANOVA interaction was modeled, the F-statistic was omitted. Effect size and source reliability were handled correctly.

criterion_1.reason: Used SSPG as primary IR marker instead of DI as specified, and no explicit DI fallback was implemented.

criterion_2.reason: Used maximum across replicates instead of mean for peak glucose, and used absolute peak rather than baseline-subtracted peak delta.

criterion_3.reason: Computed per-subject reduction as Protein - Fiber instead of the required Fiber - Protein, reversing interpretation sign.

criterion_4.reason: Ran a two-way ANOVA with interaction but did not report F-statistic, only p-value and coefficient.

criterion_5.reason: Correctly calculated partial eta-squared, categorized effect size, and interpreted clinical pattern with appropriate caveats.
